results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Every outline summary of a body unit agrees with the controlling idea of its aligned spec paragraph, in spec order (p01-p67, including the worked example after channels and the transition paragraph p57 in the Chief Architect's View); the five callout units have no spec paragraph and are not counted.

The outliner marked two units two_ideas. Introduction ¶3 (terms owned plus the chapters it builds on) and Vertical Differences ¶1 (canonical-property alerts and automotive feed lag) each realise a spec paragraph (p03, p59) whose controlling idea joins exactly these two parts; Vertical Differences ¶1 opens with a unifying sentence ('two verticals show that alert quality depends on systems outside the alert platform') that both examples serve. Neither is a stray second idea.
Every body paragraph aligns to a spec paragraph that serves one of S1-S6; no orphan paragraph.

Each figure carries a caption stating what it shows, the baseline table is introduced by the sentence saying what it shows, the metrics and channel tables carry a 'Why' column, and the bike numbers, Golf case, Eixample case and leboncoin comparison are each followed or framed by the point they make.

results.draft_locus: Architecture: A Saved-Search Store with Rebuildable Percolators ¶1
results.quote: Figure 4 shows the target architecture Ingrid's team proposes for Common Ground.
results.finding: Declared relationship is cause_effect, carrying over percolation with candidate selection and the constraint that a percolator index is a projection. The opening sentence only points at a figure; nothing says the architecture follows from the matching conclusions (why the store is the system of record and the percolators are rebuildable projections). The cause-effect link the spec's flow rationale depends on is left to the heading.

results.quote: Saved searches outlive the reference data they are written against
results.finding: Declared relationship is sequence from 'risks at the moment of matching' to 'a risk over the saved search's lifetime'. The opening states the new topic but never picks up the risk gate or the moment of matching, so the shift from matching-time to lifetime concerns is not expressed. Both flow readers could not say why the section sits here (see flow_is_followable).

All other transition_in boundaries express their declared relationship at the boundary: e.g. 'Once fan-out has decided who is notified and when' (channels), 'To size this design' (worked example), 'The cost buys speed.' (liquidity), 'An alert system is an amplifier.' (risk gate), 'The design consequence is' (p46), 'follow the same pattern' (p51), 'That pipeline now' (p66).

The introduction opens on an intriguing example (three concrete saved searches) and the Veldmark obligation; it is not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary opening, 'dawn of man' or book report.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', introduces no new subtopic or evidence beyond callbacks to the bike and Eixample case, and ends on the hand-off to Part V rather than a rephrased thesis.

It states what no section states (alerts consume every earlier Part IV surface, making discovery one pipeline that answers the part's three questions) and why it matters (that speed serves fraudsters as well as honest sellers, so it is safe only behind a risk gate and decisions every surface obeys).

The last section answers the three Part IV questions (availability, who decided position, did it lead to a contact), returns to Femke's seven-minute first contact and the 180 Eixample rentals and 41,000 alerts, and hands off to Part V and trust-and-safety-architecture.

The intro reader predicts the sections in the roadmap's order (scene, concepts incl. watchers, percolation vs re-query, store with rebuildable percolators, fan-out and channels, sizing, liquidity, risk gate, taxonomy, consent, trade-offs through questions, Part IV close), the evidence (fictional Veldmark, Rightmove and Homegate percolators, sizing arithmetic) and the tone. It does not name engine documentation or trade press, a minor gap. Note: AC-2's expected text lists sizing after consent, which disagrees with the spec's own roadmap and sections (sizing after channels); the reader agrees with the roadmap.

The AC-1 reader states the expected design: saved-search store of record with normalized versioned queries, rebuildable percolators partitioned with pre-filters, reverse matching on listing events notifying on entry with a match ledger, retraction of sold/removed listings, an orchestrator with dedup, caps, quiet hours and a send-time availability check for digests, a trust-and-safety risk gate keeping risky listings not alertable until review with stricter thresholds in rentals and a hold for new accounts' first listings; and measures latency searchable-to-provider (5 min p95), ghost-alert rate, alert-to-contact within 48h, unsubscribe and complaint rates, not sends. Dormant share appears as a lever rather than a metric, a minor gap.
